This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19
and pursuant to AB 361 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer’s Order (March 3,
2022). All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll call vote, and the vote will be
publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may observe
the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. Please view the meeting, which will be live
streamed at https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to submit
email correspondence to bsaleaumua@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may speak during the
meeting through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to speak before the item you
would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom conference
to be recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak
and downloading the Zoom application.

  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings
As a result of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, the City is under a state of local emergency, as well as
states of emergency that have been declared in the County of Los Angeles, state of California, and a federal
emergency declared by the President of the United States. In order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-
19, the City Council meeting will be open and public but conducted virtually because meeting in person would
present imminent risks to the health or safety of attendees. This way the public, the staff, and the Council will
not be physically in the same place.
The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items, which are not listed on the agenda
but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action may be taken, the Commission and staff
will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing response. Each speaker is limited to (3) three minutes. Members
of the public wishing to speak during the meeting must participate through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign
up to speak before the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom
conference to be recognized. Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak
and downloading the Zoom application.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous meeting where the public
was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not subject to public discussion at this meeting
because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final. Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous meetings are for
the purpose of memorializing the decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If discussion is desired, an item
may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or abstaining
vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent Calendar. Items excluded
from the Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent Calendar. The Commission
first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted. Public speakers shall follow the rules as set
forth under Oral Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this meeting with no final
action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment shall follow the rules
as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above are on file in the
office of the City Manager, and available upon request by emailing bsaleaumua@malibucity.org.

The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for the deaf (TDD),
please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In compliance with the Americans with

Subject:  Community Services Department Monthly Report

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file a report of activities, events, projects, and
programs coordinated by the Community Services Department during February 2022.

DISCUSSION: The Community Services Department coordinated the following activities,
projects, and programs in February 2022.

RECREATION

Aquatics: The Malibu Aquatics Foundation Seawolves Swim Team and Adult Masters
Conditioning spring programs began on February 14 with 83 participants. The spring
session of the Youth Water Polo Program in partnership with the Malibu Youth Water Polo
Foundation started on February 23. The program, instructed by Malibu High School Coach
Hayden Goldberg, meets bi-weekly and is at maximum capacity with 30 swimmers.

Community Classes: The winter session of afterschool programs ended the week of
February 28. Programs included Karate with Joey Escobar, Yoga with Little Fox Yoga,
and Science with Professor Egghead. A total of 120 students enrolled in the Malibu
Elementary School and Webster Elementary School programs, which are coordinated in
partnership with the Boys and Girls Club of Malibu.

Outdoor Recreation: Recreation staff led a full-moon hike for Malibu Elementary School
families at Charmlee Wilderness Park on February 23. Eight participants learned about
the moon's phases, nocturnal animals, and native plants.

  Page 1 of 3  Agenda Item # 3.B.2.
 Recreation Supervisor Chris Orosz led a morning hike at Charmlee Wilderness Park on
February 26 for six participants.

Recreation Guide: The Spring 2022 Recreation Guide and City Newsletter was published
online and mailed to over 9,000 addresses in the 90264 and 90265 zip-codes beginning
February 6. This was the first Recreation Guide to be printed and mailed to Malibu
residents since early 2020. Registration for Spring programs opened on February 14, and
over 194 participants pre-registered for programs.

Seniors: Weekly Senior recreation programs continued through February at Malibu Bluffs
Park, with an average of forty participants. Programs include Chair Yoga, Knitting, Mat
Yoga, and Stretch and Strength Fitness.

Recreation Coordinator Amanda Rigali hosted a Meet and Greet at Malibu Bluffs Park on
February 4. Thirty-five seniors attended the event, shared their feedback on programming
and facilities, and received Valentine's Day-themed gift bags with Malibu Senior Center
giveaways and cookies.

Community Services staff led a technology help session with six participants on February
8. Seniors received assistance with electronic devices such as iPhones and laptops.

Malibu Poet Laureate, Ann Buxie, instructed two senior poetry workshops on February 10
and 24. Four seniors wrote and shared poetry surrounding the theme "All Breathing
Things."

Skate Programs: Additional Learn to Skate Programs instructed by Champ Camp were
scheduled from January through March. The sessions were added after staff received
feedback requesting more classes, and the February session reached maximum capacity
with 18 participants.

Social Media: Department social media posts featured videos and pictures from the trail
cameras at Charmlee Wilderness Park and information about spring programs. The
Instagram stories received 515 views, a 13% increase, and 30% of the accounts reached
were Malibu residents.

Special Events: Nineteen students from Our Lady of Malibu School, Malibu Elementary
School, and Malibu High School submitted artwork for the 2022 Student Art Exhibit. The
exhibition is on display at the Art Voyagers Gallery in the Michael Landon Center and
online at Malibucity.org/StudentArtExhibit from February 14 to March 14.

Over 75 car enthusiasts attended Cars and Coffee at Malibu Bluffs Park on February 13
and 27. On February 13, event attendees had an opportunity to win gift certificates to local
restaurants by providing Super Bowl winner predictions.

Sports: The Winter Basketball program concluded on February 19 with 63 participants,
ages 6-14. The City reformatted the league to instructional conditioning classes due to the
  Page 2 of 3  Agenda Item # 3.B.2.
 Los Angeles County Department of Public Health Guidelines. Classes were held weekly
at Malibu High School and instructed by Breakthrough Sports.

PARK MAINTENANCE

Charmlee Wilderness Park: Since 2020, the City has worked with Managed Career Solutions
to complete trail clearance and remediation work at Charmlee Wilderness Park. On February
22, the City began working with a new trail crew from MCS, who will continue maintenance
and erosion control work through the end of Fiscal Year 2021-2022.

Trail crews began work on the Malibu Pacific Trail by filling areas damaged by erosion from
recent winter storms.

City staff installed bluebird box signs on eight bluebird boxes.

Equestrian Park: Completed grading of both horse arenas and added decomposed granite
(DG) in the lower parking lot.

Las Flores Park: Repaired a leaking service line to the men's restroom.

Malibu Bluffs Park: Completed renovations to the Major and Pony Baseball infields,
including tilling, adding new material, and laser leveling. Compacted clay was also added
to the pitchers' mounds and home plates areas.

Marked all irrigation sprinklers and valve boxes on the Multipurpose Field in preparation
of the temporary backstop installation for Malibu Little League's upcoming season.

Trancas Field: Work crews removed all tree tobacco and castor bean from Priority Area 1
and began removal work in Priority Area 2.

Subject:  Parks and Recreation Master Plan

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Review and discuss the Parks and Recreation Master Plan.

DISCUSSION: On June 24, 2013, the City Council approved the Parks and Recreation
Master Plan (Master Plan). The Master Plan was approved following a six-month
community outreach process to obtain community feedback on parks, recreation facilities,
programs, and their vision for the future.

The City hired a consultant to prepare the Master Plan, who used a variety of methods to
collect feedback, including interviews, a community survey, focus groups, stakeholder
meetings, and public forums. The consultant also conducted facility and program
evaluations to assess Department standards for quality and service. The community
feedback and evaluations were then used to develop priority rankings for facilities and
programs in order to highlight unmet parks and recreation-based needs.

  Facility/Amenity Priority Rankings – High Priority (Master Plan Page 68)
  1.  Walking, biking trails and greenways
  2.  Small Neighborhood Parks
  3.  Indoor Swimming Pools
  4.  Off-leash dog parks
  5.  Multi-generational Community Center
  6.  Community Gardens
  7.  Outdoor Swimming Pools
  8.  Adventure Facility (rock wall, ropes course, etc.)
  9.  Outdoor Tennis Courts

  Page 1 of 3  Agenda Item #4.A.
   Program Priority Rankings – High Priority (Master Plan Page 70)
  1.  Adult Fitness and Wellness Programs
  2.  Visual and Performing Arts Programs
  3.  Senior Programs
  4.  Open Swim Programs
  5.  Aqua Aerobics
  6.  Environmental Education Programs
  7.  Tennis Lessons and Leagues
  8.  Youth Sports Programs

The Master Plan also provided a wealth of other metrics, including demographics,
strengths, opportunities for improvement, and key findings.

At the January 19, 2022 Special meeting, the Commission reviewed the Master Plan and
requested additional information regarding the use of Los Angeles County Library
Set Aside Funds as well as information regarding the potential use of the Heathercliff
Property for a community swimming pool.

Library Set Aside Funds
The Malibu Public Library (Library) is owned and operated by the County of Los Angeles
(County), with services paid for from a portion of residential property taxes. Malibu
residents contribute a larger amount in property tax than what is spent on local library
services. In response to this inequity, the County and the City established a Memorandum
of Understanding (MOU) that establishes that the County will set aside the difference
between the amount of property tax revenue generated by Malibu residents for County
library services and Library expenses into a designated fund for Library-related expenses.
In Fiscal Year 2020-2021, it was estimated that the beginning balance for the Set Aside
Fund would be approximately $13.5 million in Fiscal Year 2022-2023.

The City and County work cooperatively to determine how the Set Aside Funds will be
spent each Fiscal Year. In the recent past, Set Aside Fund expenditures have included
enhanced service hours and library collections, hiring additional library staff, and the
Library Speaker Series.

A Library Needs Assessment (Needs Assessment) was completed in 2005 to optimize the
allocation of the Set Aside Funds. The Needs Assessment primarily focused on the large-
scale renovation of the existing Library as well as the purchase of new furniture and
equipment to serve the Library. The Malibu Library Renovation was completed in 2012.

In 2017, the Council authorized an update to the 2005 Library Needs Assessment to
establish new service goals and guide the management of the funding in future years
driven by community input. In 2018, the City Council accepted the findings of the Needs
Assessment study and authorized staff to work with the County on several new initiatives
including analyzing the feasibility of expanding library services on the west side of Malibu.
In the aftermath of the Woolsey Fire and onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, City priorities
  Page 2 of 3  Agenda Item #4.A.
 shifted to public safety and rebuilding, and the Council postponed new projects related to
the Library.

Staff reviewed the possibility of utilizing a portion of the Set Aside Funds for a potential
project. The Set Aside Funds could be used for a project, provided the project has a nexus
to the library. Any proposed project would require approval from the City Council and the
County. An analysis of resources, funding, need, and demographics would likely also be
required.

Heathercliff Property
Staff worked with the Planning Department and City geotechnical consultant reviewers
regarding the possibility of utilizing the Heathercliff property for a community swimming
pool. The size of the property would most likely accommodate a community swimming
pool; however, further technical studies would be required before an official
determination can be made. Additionally, the property is zoned as Commercial
Neighborhood (CN) which does not allow public recreation facilities or amenities, such
as swimming pools, community centers, sandboxes, slides, swings, and sport courts. A
change in the property's zoning designation would be required to permit a public
recreation facility. The change in zoning designation would require approval by the
Planning Commission and City Council, as well as a Local Coastal Program Amendment
for the permitted uses table.

The CN zoning designation does allow for parks, beaches, and playgrounds with a
Conditional Use Permit; however, the definition of parks, beaches, and playgrounds is
unclear in the City of Malibu Municipal Code and Local Implementation Plan. Planning
Department staff recommends requesting a Determination of Use from the Planning
Commission to determine if the proposed use is consistent with the zoning designation or
if the project site would need to be rezoned, should a park project without a public
recreation facility be recommended.

The Commission may discuss the Master Plan and determine possible recommendations
for Council consideration.

Subject:  Park Enhancement and Donation Program

RECOMMENDED ACTION: 1) Review the recommended revisions to the Park
Enhancement and Donation Program; and 2) Recommend City Council approve the
revisions.

DISCUSSION: On January 10, 2018, the City Council approved the Park Enhancement
and Beautification Program (Program)(Attachment 1) for City parks and facilities following
a recommendation from the Commission. The Program provides guidelines for the
acceptance of private donations and memorial items, such as benches, rocks, and trees,
to be placed at City parks and recreation facilities. The Program also established a limit
on the number of memorial items placed in each park.

  Location  Maximum Allowed Items  Current Items
  Las Flores Creek Park  4  0
  Malibu Bluffs Park  20  20
  Trancas Canyon Park  4  1
  Legacy Park  0  0

The Commission did not recommend allowing memorial items at Legacy Park due to the
theme and character of the park and its amenities. Additionally, Charmlee Wilderness Park
was not included as the City was in the middle of a five-year reciprocal lease agreement
with the Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority, which oversaw the park at that
time.

Since the Program’s inception, the Department has received several requests each year
to install memorial items at Malibu Bluffs Park, Legacy Park, and Charmlee Wilderness
Park. Additional items may be installed if approved by the Commission and City Council.

  Page 1 of 2  Agenda Item #5.A.
 In early 2022, staff reviewed the Program and prepared recommended revisions for
Commission review. Many of the benches at Legacy Park have commemorative or
memorial inlaid tiles that were installed when the park opened in 2011 (Attachment 2).
Charmlee Wilderness Park has one memorial bench located at the end of the Potrero Trail
near the reservoir lookout.

Staff recommends the following revisions to the Program:

  -  Allow up to five additional memorial inlaid tiles in the same or substantially similar
  style on vacant benches at Legacy Park
  -  Add Charmlee Wilderness Park to include a maximum of 5 memorial items with the
  current bench and four additional items in the area near the nature center

Staff does not recommend allowing additional items at Malibu Bluffs Park due to the large
number of items already installed. If the Commission approves a recommendation to
revise the Program, staff will take the recommendation to the City Council for final
approval.

  Park Enhancement and Donation Program
Community organizations and individuals may donate money and needed equipment to the City
of Malibu for park enhancements and beautification projects. The City accepts enhancements
such as benches, native plants, trees or other items which can be earmarked for a specific project
taking place at City parks or facilities.

All donations become the property of the City of Malibu to oversee, maintain and manage. Over
time, a park may be redesigned or renovated which may require the removal or relocation of a
donated item. The City will determine how to manage a donation with no guarantee to retain the
item during any length of time. The City will make every effort to notify the donor if the item is
removed, relocated, replaced, etc. It is the donor’s responsibility to notify the City if their contact
information has changed.

The following must be approved by the Community Services Director:
   The need of the item or equipment
   The make, model and type of item or equipment
   The installation location of the item or equipment
   Donor recognition

A limited amount of memorial items and donations are permitted at each park. Once the park
reaches the maximum capacity on items, additional items will not be accepted unless reviewed
by the Parks and Recreation Commission and approved by City Council.

  Location  Total Items/Enhancements
  Las Flores Creek Park  4
  Malibu Bluffs Park  20
  Trancas Canyon Park  4
  Legacy Park  0

Once a memorial item or donation is approved, costs are determined and payment is received,
City staff will order the item or equipment and install it at the identified facility. Ongoing
maintenance and upkeep of the equipment or materials shall become the City’s responsibility.

Modifications to existing facilities which provide a significant visual, functional or land use change
may require special permits and must be approved by the City of Malibu Planning Department.

 POLICY

A. General Provisions for Donated Items

  1. A donation must be consistent with the needs of City parks and facilities.

  2. A donation must provide benefit to the City and the community.

  3. A cost analysis will be performed prior to the acceptance of the donation to insure the
  cost associated with the item does not outweigh the value to the City. The City retains
  the right to refuse a donation if the cost exceeds the community benefit.

  4. Donated items must be in safe, durable and usable condition.

  5. Donated items that are intended for an exclusive user group or that are associated with
  a specific group will require approval before a donation can be made.

  6. Once a donated item has been accepted it becomes City property. The City may replace
  or dispose of the item as it deems appropriate.

  7. Facility naming rights will only be approved by City Council.

B. Facility Donations

  1. The donation must fit the style or current aesthetic plan of the facility.

  2. Permanent modifications to facilities will only be approved by City Council.

  3. The City reserves the right to limit or deny donations based on the need and available
  space.

C. Acknowledgment of Donor

  1. Donor acknowledgment requests that will be permanently displayed with or on the
  donated item will be considered under the guidelines:
  a. The plaque or plate will be placed on the item or near it at the City’s discretion
  b. The plaque or plate will not be obtrusive or detract from the donated item
  c. The message on the plaque or plate will be limited to name, date and a short
  phrase
  d. The City will approve the written message on the plaque or plate
  e. The plaque or plate will be maintained by the City for a total length of 7 years after
  the donation. If the plaque or plate is damaged or missing after 7 years, the City
  retains the right to remove it without a replacement

  2

  5.A. Attachment 1
   2. In the event a location for a plaque or plate is not feasible, City staff will work with the
  donor to determine alternative recognition options.
D. Payments and Processing

  The City requests payments for benches, trees, rocks and equipment be made in full. The
  City will not order any items until the full payment is received and processed. The City
  will provide the donor with an invoice along with a Tax Identification number.

  Installation will be completed in 4 months or less.

CITY FACILITIES, PARKS AND NEEDS
The City will allow donations to be made for the facilities and parks listed below. The items listed
with the facility are the highest needs or options for donations. The City restricts the number of
memorial donations at each location. The list will be updated on an ongoing basis.

MINUTES
  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  SPECIAL MEETING
  MARCH 22, 2022
  VARIO US TELECONFERENCE LOCATIONS
  5:30P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Vice Chair Skophammer called the meeting to order at 5:38 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance via teleconference by the Recording
  Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Alicia Peak {atTived at 6:10 p.m.); Vice Chair Dane Skophammer; and
  Commissioners Georgia Goldfarb, Suzanne Guldimann, and Judy Villablanca

  ALSO PRESENT: Jesse Bobbett, Community Services Director; Kristin Riesgo,
  Community Services Deputy Director; and Loren Davis, Recreation Coordinator

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Vice Chair Skophammer led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Guldimann moved, and Commissioner Villablanca seconded a
  motion to approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-
  0, Chair Peak absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recreation Coordinator Davis reported the agenda for the meeting was posted on
  March 17, 2022.

ITEMl  CEREMONIAL/PRESENT ATIO NS

  None.

ITEM2  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  None.

ITEM3  CONSENT CALENDAR
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Special Meeting
  Minutes of March 22, 2022
  Page 2 of6

MOTION  Commissioner Villablanca moved, and Commissioner Goldfarb seconded a motion
  to approve the Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried
  4-0, Chair Peak absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the February 15, 2022
  Parks and Recreation Commission Regular meeting.
  2.  Community Services Department Monthly Report
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report of activities, events,
  projects, and programs coordinated by the Community Services Department
  during February 2022.

ITEM4  OLD BUSINESS

  A.  Parks and Recreation Master Plan
  Recommended Action: Review and discuss the Parks and Recreation Master
  Plan.

  Community Services Director Bobbett presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Goldfarb stated the Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District
  (SMMUSD) planned to construct a new pool at Malibu High School.

  Commissioner Villablanca stated the City would be required to pay SMMUSD to
  utilize a pool and availability would remain limited due to school hours and sports
  team usage.

  In response to Commissioner Villablanca, Community Services Director Bobbett
  stated if the Commission requested a rezoning of the Heathercliff property, the
  Planning Commission would likely want to know specific details regarding the
  proposed project during their review of the request. He also stated certain facilities
  and amenities could be permitted with a Conditional Use Permit.

  Commissioner Guldimann stated the Heathercliff property was earmarked for a
  park and inquired about the best way to move forward.

  In response to Commissioner Villablanca, Commissioner Guldimann stated the Iok:i
  property could be used for a pool, but the property contained elevation changes and
  parking could be a concern due to the neighboring Santa Monica College satellite
  campus.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Special Meeting
  Minutes of March 22, 2022
  Page 3 of 6

Vice Chair Skophammer stated the Commission should keep moving forward on
the project and suggested approaching City Council to rezone the Heathercliff
property for a community center and pool.

Commissioner Guldimann indicated agreement with Vice Chair Skophammer and
suggested modular buildings to reduce costs.

Vice Chair Skophammer stated community need should be the priority over costs.

Melissa Stallings, Malibu Library Manager, stated the Parks Master Plan and
Library Needs Assessment both contain information regarding a community needs
assessment. She recommended the Commission review the Parks Master Plan and
stated a community center with multi-generational activities and library services in
western Malibu were identified as community needs.

In response to Commissioner Villablanca, Community Services Director Bobbett
stated Elizabeth Shavelson, Assistant to the City Manager, was the staff liaison to
the Library Subcommittee and was working with them to analyze the feasability of
expanding library services in western Malibu based on direction from the Council.

At 6: 10 p.m., Chair Peak joined the meeting.

In response to Commissioner Villablanca, Ms. Stallings stated the Library
Subcommittee would meet in spring 2022 to discuss Fiscal Year 2022-2023
projects and the library set aside funds.

Commissioner Villablanca suggested the Commission discuss the project with the
Library Subcommittee for their input. She stated support from the Library
Subcommittee would back the Commission's recommendation when approaching
City Council for their approval.

Commissioner Villablanca stated a community center, a pool, and a satellite library
on the Heathercliff property should be the top priorities.

Commissioner Guldimann indicated agreement with Commissioner Villablanca.

Commissioner Goldfarb stated she supported approaching the Library
Subcommittee to obtain a recommendation for City Council consideration. She
stated the Commission should review the Parks Master Plan and Library Needs
Assessment.

In response to Chair Peak, Ms. Stallings stated the Almaden Community Center in
San Jose was a joint-use facility with library services.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Special Meeting
  Minutes of March 22, 2022
  Page 4 of 6

  Community Services Director Bobbett recommended approaching the Library
  Subcommittee first to determine if a joint-use facility with a library component was
  desired. He stated the Commission should have a clear plan and recommendation
  for the Subcommittee.

  In response to Chair Peak, Commissioner Guldimann stated the Commission
  should focus on incorporating a library component into any plans for a community
  center.

  Vice Chair Skophammer clarified the project should include a building that offers
  library services.

  Commissioner Guldimann indicated agreement with Vice Chair Skophammer and
  stated a community center would be more appealing than a stand-alone pool.

  In response to Vice Chair Skophammer, Community Services Director Bobbett
  stated the best approach would be to go before the Library Subcommittee regarding
  a library component before going before the City Council.

  In response to Chair Peak, Community Services Director Bobbett stated staff would
  discuss the best process for presenting the idea for a multi-generational recreation
  center with a pool and library services to the Library Subcommittee.

ITEMS  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Park Enhancement and Donation Program
  Recommended Action: 1) Review the recommended revisions to the Park
  Enhancement and Donation Program; and 2) Recommend City Council approve
  the revisions.

  Community Services Director Bobbett presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Guldimann stated Charmlee Wilderness Park and Legacy Park
  should not be included in the Park Enhancement Donation Program.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Community Services Director Bobbett
  stated the memorial plaques were flush with the back of the benches at Legacy Park.

  In response to Chair Peak, Commissioner Guldimann stated there were multiple
  requests for memorial items at parks and by limiting the number of items, staff
  could deny requests.

  Commissioner Villablanca indicated agreement with Commissioner Guldimann.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Special Meeting
  Minutes of March 22, 2022
  Page 5 of 6

  In response to Commissioner Villablanca, Community Services Director Bobbett
  stated the Park Enhancement and Donation Program included trees and plants, but
  most people preferred to donate benches or rocks.

MOTION  Commissioner Villablanca moved, and Commissioner Guldimann recommended a
  motion to make no changes to the Park Enhancement and Donation Program. The
  question was called, and the motion carried 4-1, Chair Peak dissenting.

ITEM6  STAFF UPDATES

  Community Services Deputy Director Riesgo provided an update on Charmlee
  Wilderness Park, Trancas Field, part-time staff recruitment, and skate boarding
  programs.

  Community Services Director Bobbett provided an update on staff assignments
  from the Commission.

ITEM7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Chair Peak requested the Commission place an item on the April 19, 2022 Regular
  meeting agenda regarding the Department's Financial Assistance Program.

  In response to Commissioner Guldimann, Community Services Deputy Director
  Riesgo stated Commissioners were welcome to attend Chumash Day on April 9,
  2022.

  In response to Vice Chair Skophammer, Community Services Deputy Director
  Riesgo stated the restrooms at Trancas Park were locked by contractors and she
  would speak with the Parks Division to see if they were aware of any issues.

  In response to Vice Chair Skophammer, Community Services Director Bobbett
  stated he would research options for installing Wi-Fi at Trancas Canyon Park.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  Parks Master Plan
  Scholarship Assistance Program

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION  At 7:39 p.m., Vice Chair Skophammer moved, and Chair Peak seconded a motion
  to adjourn the meeting. The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.
